Preparation_Method: Thin-film hydration: dissolve Span 60, cholesterol, and DSPE-PEG(2000) maleimide in chloroform; add 100 µL QDs dispersed in chloroform; evaporate solvent to form a thin film; hydrate with 1.0 mL CA-MIONs aqueous solution at 60 °C for 60 min; extrude through 0.4 µm and 0.1 µm filters; centrifuge at 11,000 rpm for 15 min and redisperse the sediment in water.

Standardization_Status: Standardized fractions computed among vesicle-forming components only (phospholipids, sterols, surfactants, charge inducers, PEG-lipids, fatty acids); drug, solvents, buffers and coating polymers excluded
Surface_Modification: Transferrin coupled to maleimide groups on PEG chains via a thioether linkage
Preparation_Method: Prepare PEGNIO/QDs/MIONs by thin-film hydration, extrusion, and centrifugation. Thiolate 5 nmol Tf with 25 nmol Traut’s reagent in 500 µL HEPES EDTA buffer (30 mM HEPES and 0.1 mM EDTA, pH 8.5) for 2 h at room temperature; wash with HEPES pH 6.5 and concentrate to 200 µL. Add thiolated Tf to the niosomes and incubate for 24 h at 4 °C.
Key_Findings: Tf decoration enhanced U87 cell uptake; combined with magnetic treatment, the formulation provided dual targeting and fluorescence/MRI imaging.

Standardization_Status: Standardized fractions computed among vesicle-forming components only (phospholipids, sterols, surfactants, charge inducers, PEG-lipids, fatty acids); drug, solvents, buffers and coating polymers excluded; molar fractions not computed (missing MW for one or more components, or unit not mass)

Preparation_Method: Prepare HAS-LIP by thin-film hydration and ultrasonication. Coat with 0.6% CH solution (1:1, v/v; pH 5.5), stir for 1 h and sonicate for 7 min. Role_In_Paper: solvent for CH and SA solutions

Drug_Loading_EE_DL: Oxp: entrapment efficiency 26.4%; drug loading 0.66 μg/10^6 CFUs. MTZ: entrapment efficiency 29.7%; drug loading 0.75 μg/10^6 CFUs.

Preparation_Method: Thin-film hydration: dissolve lipid materials in chloroform; add an aqueous solution of Oxp and MTZ dropwise under water-bath ultrasound to form a W/O emulsion; remove chloroform by rotary evaporation, add water and incubate at 45 °C for 1 h. Key_Findings: CBS conjugation with CS-coated Oxp/MTZ liposomes enabled colon-specific release and increased liposome accumulation at the colorectal cancer site. Reported size and zeta potential are for CBS-CS@Lipo/Oxp/MTZ.

Drug_Loading_EE_DL: DOX feed: 1 mg DOX/10 mol. of phospholipid; encapsulation efficiency not reported.

Preparation_Method: Lipids were dissolved in chloroform and deposited as a thin film under reduced pressure and nitrogen. The film was hydrated with 250 mM ammonium sulfate at pH 4 at 55 °C, then sonicated for 2 h. Unentrapped ammonium sulfate was removed by Sephadex G-75 gel chromatography. DOX dissolved in HEPS buffer at pH 7.4 was added, and the mixture was incubated for 1 h at 55 °C under reduced pressure for pH-gradient loading. Unencapsulated DOX was removed by gel chromatography. For lyophilization, the liposome pellet was added to 10% lactose monohydrate solution, frozen at −70 °C, and freeze-dried for 24 h.
Key_Findings: Lyophilized liposomes showed improved storage stability. In vitro, laser exposure at 30 J released 33.6% of encapsulated DOX immediately and about 95% by 20 h post-irradiation. In mice, DOX-loaded liposomes combined with diode laser treatment inhibited tumor growth.
Evidence_Location: Methods, “Liposomes preparation and drug encapsulation” and “Liposomes lyophilization and characterization”; Results, “Characteristics of the lyophilized liposomes” and “Effect of irradiation with continuous wave diode laser.”

Standardization_Status: Standardized fractions computed among vesicle-forming components only (phospholipids, sterols, surfactants, charge inducers, PEG-lipids, fatty acids); drug, solvents, buffers and coating polymers excluded; molar fractions not computed (missing MW for one or more components, or unit not mass)
Size_PDI_Zeta: Particle size: 192.0 ± 69.9 nm; PDI: 0.15 ± 0.06; zeta potential: −33.8 ± 5.7 mV
Preparation_Method: Thin membrane dispersion: dissolve soybean phospholipid, Tween-80, and POD in chloroform; evaporate to form a thin film, vacuum-dry overnight, hydrate with LC-DCA aqueous solution at 35 °C for 0.5 h, sonicate in an ice-water bath for 8 min, and extrude through a 0.45 μm membrane.
Key_Findings: At more than 60 mg LC-DCA, particle size increased, PDI increased, a bimodal size distribution appeared, and EE decreased. Elasticity was 15.1 ± 0.5.
